title: Healthtech procurement response: evidence map for AI, GDPR and cloud questions
summary: A synthetic no-personal-data map for six evidence gates: intended use, data boundary, security evidence, procurement response, cloud/LLM economics and decision stop rule.
answer: European healthtech teams can make procurement responses easier to review by assigning a dated owner and evidence source to intended use, personal-data boundaries, security questions, procurement claims, cloud/LLM economics and the final reversible decision or stop rule.
boundary: Not legal advice, an AI Act or GDPR compliance opinion, security assessment, vendor recommendation, certification, customer case study, ranking, demand, savings, ROI or revenue claim.
